security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed a critical unverified remote bootstrap command in both installation documents that downloads and executes remote code with TLS verification disabled. Beyond that, most static hits are false positives from Markdown, documented scoped credentials, and standard shell patterns; added intent-level findings cover external skill/instruction-path injection risk and credentialed artifact uploads lacking authorization. Overall the skill is primarily coordination documentation but requires hardening before publication.

remediation.issue: Remote code is downloaded and executed during installation with TLS verification disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the curl-to-Node bootstrap command. Distribute a versioned artifact with a published checksum or signature, and require normal TLS verification.

remediation.issue: External skills can be imported from mutable sources.
remediation.suggestion: Require a pinned commit or content digest and an explicit confirmation before installing an external skill.

remediation.issue: The port troubleshooting command can stop an unrelated process.
remediation.suggestion: Display the resolved process details and require explicit confirmation, or use the managed Paperclip stop command.

remediation.issue: External skills and absolute instruction paths can inject agent-controlling instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Default-deny external skill import; require human approval and commit-SHA or content-hash pinning, and canonicalize instruction paths to approved workspace roots.

remediation.issue: Artifact uploads use injected credentials without authorization or content classification.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict uploads to workspace paths, add sensitive-content scanning, and require explicit authorization before upload.

remediation.issue: The skill lacks an explicit rule that issue text, comments, artifacts, and fetched files are untrusted data.
remediation.suggestion: Add a non-negotiable instruction to never follow directives found in task content or external sources unless independently authorized by task and policy.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Remote Bootstrap Code Execution
semantic_findings.description: The installation instructions disable TLS verification, download a base64-encoded remote payload, and execute it with Node. The payload has no checksum, signature, or pinned immutable source.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both duplicated installation documents contain the complete download-to-execution pipeline with insecure TLS and no integrity control.

semantic_findings.title: External Skill Import as Indirect Instruction Injection
semantic_findings.description: Company skills are instruction-bearing agent control files that can be imported from external URLs, GitHub, local paths, or raw source strings, and the heartbeat treats issue text, comments, and wake payloads as work context without an explicit rule that such content is untrusted data rather than authority. This combination allows externally supplied instructions to influence agent behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The import mechanism and untrusted-context handling are documented, but no exploit is embedded; the risk depends on operator policy and source pinning.

semantic_findings.title: Credentialed Artifact Upload Without Authorization or Content Classification
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs automatic upload of workspace files to the Paperclip issue using injected credentials, and the helper script accepts any regular local file with no path-root restriction, secret classification, or explicit user confirmation. A sensitive file could be uploaded without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The upload path and lack of gating are clear from the script, but data exposure depends on which file the agent selects, so intent is not conclusively malicious.

content.value_statement: Teams need a consistent way to coordinate agent tasks, approvals, and updates. This skill guides Paperclip API workflows with clear status and governance steps.
actual_capabilities: Check agent assignments and issue context through Paperclip API workflows.
Check out tasks before work and update their status with a run audit header.
Post progress comments and create or manage child tasks for delegated work.
Handle approval follow-up and execution-policy review steps.
Configure recurring Paperclip routines and review workspace guidance.
Upload generated deliverables as issue attachments with the included helper script.
limitations: It coordinates Paperclip work and does not perform the underlying domain work by itself.
It requires a running Paperclip instance and valid Paperclip environment variables.
It cannot bypass company boundaries, approvals, budgets, or API authorization.
Installation instructions require review because one bootstrap command executes unverified remote code.

use_cases.title: Manage assigned engineering work
use_cases.description: Check out an assigned issue, record progress, and move it to the correct review state.

use_cases.title: Coordinate multi-agent delivery
use_cases.description: Create child tasks, monitor dependencies, and leave durable updates for other agents.

use_cases.title: Review approval decisions
use_cases.description: Process approval-linked issues and document approval or change-request outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Check my assignments
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Paperclip assignments and summarize the next actionable task.

prompt_templates.title: Start a task safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Check out my current Paperclip task, read its heartbeat context, and post a short progress update.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a dependency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Paperclip task for blockers. Create child tasks only when needed and document the owner and next action.

prompt_templates.title: Complete an approval review
prompt_templates.prompt: Process the pending Paperclip approval, review linked issues, and update each issue with the correct decision and audit trail.

output: Next step: Review the latest stakeholder comment before editing.
Update posted: The task remains blocked until approval is recorded.
Artifact uploaded to the current issue
Work product marked ready for review
Final comment includes the attachment link.

best_practices: Check out a task before starting work and include the run ID on every modifying request.
Read scoped wake context and new comments before broad task or repository exploration.
Leave durable progress in comments or work products before ending a heartbeat.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for domain work that belongs in a coding, research, or writing skill.
Do not retry a checkout conflict or advance another participant’s review stage.
Do not copy Paperclip API keys or bridge tokens into prompts, logs, comments, or documents.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages Paperclip tasks, assignments, comments, approvals, routines, and coordination workflows.

faq.question: Does it write application code?
faq.answer: No. It coordinates Paperclip work. Use a domain-specific skill for implementation work.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: A running Paperclip environment provides API URL, API key, agent, company, and run context variables.

faq.question: How does it prevent duplicate work?
faq.answer: It requires task checkout and instructs agents to stop after a 409 conflict.

faq.question: Can it upload deliverables?
faq.answer: Yes. The included helper uploads a selected workspace file to the current issue and creates a work product.

faq.question: Should I use the installation bootstrap command?
faq.answer: Review it first. The documented remote bootstrap command executes unverified code and should be replaced with a verified installation method.
